title: Inner StateMachines' reliance on reset pose for `End` state causes issues, when using `Root` type
body: ### Tested versions Current master, has been a problem since 4.3 at least, when I first noticed. ### System information Godot v4.6.rc2 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.91 GiB memory ### Issue description Any `Root` StateMachine placed inside another becomes very troublesome to use because of its tendency to cause a T pose in the character on the way out, especially if via an `At End` transition. This sporadically results in an unavoidable 1 frame T pose in an unblended transition, or a brief pulling of the character to a T pose in a blended animation. It's also so unpredictable in its occurrence that it may as well be a bug. However, much more often, when a "Root" StateMachine's inner length or outer transition conditions aren't managed with frame-perfect accuracy, we get this: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/becdbcc8-114c-43f0-845f-fc0d7ec3d083 In the demonstration above, I've forced it to occur by having a sync transition from one shorter "static impact" animation leading to end, mixed with another "moving impact" animation that has a different length, that I trigger by moving my character mid-animation. This leaves the animation momentarily stranded inside the inner statemachine, resulting in a T pose on exit. While the above is reproducible, I've found this T pose to randomly occur when leaving any nested `Root` state machine with a similar configuration often, even when by all accounts unwarranted. It would be vastly more preferable in these situations to do what `Nested` StateMachines do, and just freeze the animation on the last frame of whatever animation in the StateMachine led to the End state, instead of treating End as a reset. The above is all with `Reset Ends` disabled too, so I'm clueless what that option is supposed to do. ### Steps to reproduce I haven't been able to reliably reproduce the single frame T-pose in a situations when it shouldn't occur, however the purpose of this issue is to say that using the T pose at all instead of just treating the last frame of the last animation as the `End` pose for an inner StateMachine is really troublesome. The MRP can demonstrate the reset pose's unneeded presence via a stalled `At End` transition. 1. Download and start MRP. 2. Observe the reset pose of the box, at top-left, relative to the camera. 3. Play the game. 4. The box starts moving from the center of the screen to the top right, while syncing into a longer animation that takes it to the middle right. 5. This animation reaches its conclusion and freezes in place, in the middle right. 6. Pressing spacebar allows it to meet its `At End` condition, and then move from the middle right to the bottom. If the spacebar is pressed well in advance, we see this: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04fff9fe-165b-4331-836a-6716c54cec86 However, if the spacebar is pressed after the inner statemachine is frozen, awaiting the transition to "End", we get this: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b86b930c-4381-4ee9-8ace-839e72f50200 ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [statemachine-reset-end-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24855153/statemachine-reset-end-mrp.zip)
